ai.description: *Megophrys dzukou* is a small frog (28–32 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark, V-shaped markings. It features distinct dermal projections on the upper eyelids and a prominent, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys dzukou* is best distinguished by the distinct, elongated, horn-like dermal projection on each upper eyelid, which is significantly more prominent than in other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys dzukou* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shrublands in the Dzükou Valley, typically found at elevations between 2,400 and 2,600 meters.
ai.behavior: *Megophrys dzukou* is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter during the day to ambush small invertebrates with its cryptic, leaf-like appearance.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys dzukou* breeds in streams during the monsoon season (June–August). Females lay small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys dzukou* is endemic to the Dzükou Valley in the Nagaland-Manipur border region of Northeast India, occurring at elevations between 2,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Megophrys dzukou* emits a series of short, metallic "tink" notes at a high pitch, typically heard from vegetation near fast-flowing streams in high-altitude forests.
